title: Actionist AssemblyPlan
design_note: The AssemblyPlan is the output of the deterministic composer for ONE application revision. It is NOT a new contract family. It CONSUMES the S2-L1 (P04) module contract family `actionist:p04:module-contract-family:v1` by reference and adds exactly three things that family does not own: (1) the solver verdict and its named unsatisfied constraint, (2) the ordered set of BindingPlans selected from a pre-verified feasible set, and (3) the composition-level budgets and residues. Every enum below that also appears in P04 is imported verbatim; a divergence is a defect, not a dialect. The AssemblyPlan never edits a CapabilityContract, never mints authority, and never records a compatibility judgement a model made.

renamed_to_avoid_collision.p03_supply_verdict_UNDERDETERMINED: P03 uses the string UNDERDETERMINED as a SUPPLY-CENSUS verdict about a capability kind (e.g. `portal`). The solver's UNDERDETERMINED is a per-composition CONTRACT-DEFECT verdict. They are different objects with the same spelling. This schema never reads a P03 supply verdict into `solver_verdict`; the shelf-side value travels as `candidate.supply_census_verdict` and is advisory only.

assembly_id.description: Stable identity for this assembly attempt, including rejected attempts. An INFEASIBLE result still mints an assembly_id: a refusal is a recorded result, not an absence.

revision.description: Composition revision. A new revision never mutates a prior AssemblyPlan; prior revisions are retained because the eval suite scores verdict stability across identical inputs (K6 determinism kill).

product_spec_ref.description: P02 explicitly deferred the minimum ProductSpec to this lane: 'The minimum cannot be closed until S2-L4 defines what the composer consumes.' These are the ONLY ProductSpec fields the solver reads. Everything else in a ProductSpec is for humans and for acceptance, not for feasibility.

consumed_fields.description: The composer-consumed minimum. Stated as a closed list so P02 can freeze its schema against a real consumer.

requirements.description: EARS-slotted requirements. The solver reads only `atom`, `authority` and `coverage`; it does NOT parse response prose.

atom.description: One of the 12 solution atoms. Free-text atoms are a spec defect, not a composer problem.

entities.description: Client vocabulary is preserved verbatim. The solver uses entities only to detect identity/data conflicts, never to rename donor tables.

data_mode.description: Phase 8 §6.1 monotonic ladder, retained verbatim. Ordering: ui_only < read_only_external < api_only < owned_postgres.

open_markers.description: P02 promotion gate. The composer REFUSES to plan against a spec with open_markers > 0 unless a recorded waiver exists; it does not silently resolve a marker.

host_contract_version.description: Pinned P04 HostContract version. A module declaring requires_host against a different version is a `host_version` conflict, not a warning.

solver.description: The deterministic result. This object is produced with NO model in the loop. If any field here was produced by a model, the plan is void.

input_digest.description: Digest over the canonicalised (candidate pool + host contract + consumed spec fields). Two runs with the same input_digest MUST yield the same verdict, or K6 fires.

checks_run.description: Every constraint evaluated, in order, with its outcome. A check that did not run is `not_run`, never absent — silence must not read as a pass.

missing_field.description: Required when outcome=underdetermined. Names the contract field whose absence made the check undecidable. This is the mechanism that turns a solver failure into a P04 contract bug report.

infeasible_reason.description: Required and non-null when verdict=INFEASIBLE. EXACTLY ONE named constraint. Reaching INFEASIBLE with the wrong reason scores as a failure because the reason selects the next gate.

relaxations_applied.description: Solver honesty rule (Phase 8 §6.3): the solver may NEVER relax a constraint to be helpful. A solver that degrades gracefully is indistinguishable from a broken one. Any value other than 0 voids the plan.

tie_break_rule.description: Named, stable, total ordering used when two feasible sets are otherwise equal. Must be deterministic (e.g. lexicographic capability_id). Random or timestamp tie-breaks void determinism.

authority_ceiling.description: Session ceiling declared at spec time. P04 C4: the composition's authority scope is the INTERSECTION of member scopes, never the union.

candidate_pool.description: Every candidate considered, INCLUDING those eliminated. Silent truncation reads as full coverage, so drops are recorded, not omitted.

supply_census_verdict.description: Advisory P03 shelf verdict (commodity | scarce | product_layer_missing_under_permissive_terms | UNDERDETERMINED). NEVER read into solver.verdict.

retrieval_layer.description: L4 (lexical/embedding) is advisory ONLY: it may widen the pool, may never satisfy a port and may never remove a candidate.

candidates_dropped_at_cap.description: Count truncated by the top-k cap. Recorded always, including when zero.

feasible_sets.description: Pre-verified alternatives handed to the model plane. The model chooses AMONG these and may not add to them. Empty when verdict != FEASIBLE.

selected_set.description: Null unless verdict=FEASIBLE and a chooser ran. `chosen_by` records WHO chose, so a model choice is never mistaken for a deterministic one.

escalation_trigger.description: Named triggers only. Discretionary escalation is forbidden because it makes cost unpredictable and eval results uninterpretable.

bindings.description: Ordered BindingPlan references. The BindingPlan OBJECT is owned by P04; this plan holds references plus composition-level ordering and the checks that only make sense across bindings.

migration_authority.description: Exactly one named owner per resource (P04 C6, INV-P09-1). Two bindings claiming one resource is `namespace`, not a merge.

glue_budget.description: Composition-level budget. P04 owns the per-binding glue_budget; this is the sum plus the composition ceiling. Overflow is a named INFEASIBLE constraint, not a warning, because 'a change set exceeding the ratio is a rewrite wearing a codemod's clothes'.

underdetermined.description: The UNDERDETERMINED channel. A15: unknown compatibility returns UNDERDETERMINED; it never becomes model confidence. Each entry is simultaneously a blocker for THIS plan and a defect report against the named contract field.

field.description: Dotted path of the missing/undecidable contract field, e.g. `PackagingProfile.rights_state`.

consumes.description: Contract family / spec ids this plan was solved against, pinned by version.

solver_verdict.description: Three verdicts, retained verbatim from Phase 8 §6.2. FEASIBLE = at least one set satisfies every check. INFEASIBLE = a declared constraint is violated (the contracts were sufficient to decide NO). UNDERDETERMINED = the declared contracts are insufficient to decide either way; this is a CONTRACT DEFECT and is reported to S2-L1, not resolved by guessing.

feasibility_class.description: A set can be feasible yet still require a named human gate (e.g. licence obligation review). Collapsing these would let a human-gated set look automatic.

candidate_disposition.description: Every candidate ends in exactly one disposition. `quarantined` is distinct from `eliminated`: it means rights or security state forbids consideration at all.

unsatisfied_constraint.description: Phase 8 defined the first ten. This lane adds nine, each because a Sprint 1 packet proved a real failure the original ten could not name: `identity` (INV-P10-1 sole identity authority), `navigation` (INV-P10-4/5/6), `migration_owner` (P04 C6 / INV-P09-1 — distinct from `namespace`, which is about collision; this is about contested AUTHORITY), `tenancy` (INV-P09-7 / INV-P11-3 tenant key from first migration), `rollback` (I-P14-1 multi-object, I-P14-2 horizon), `host_version` (P04 requires_host pinning), `glue_budget` (adaptation_unbounded), `observability_identity` (P04 C7 stable capability id), `evidence_tier` (I-P15-2 min-gate, never averaged).

authority_level.description: Phase 8 §7.1 authority ladder, retained verbatim and strictly ordered. P04's CapabilityContract.authority_class (read_only | tenant_scoped_write | external_effecting | privileged) is a CAPABILITY-shaped classification; this is a SESSION-shaped ceiling. The mapping between them is given in compatibility-and-authority-rules.json and must not be assumed.

runtime_profile.description: P14 §6, five profiles derived from reuse shape rather than chosen. sidecar_service is the only profile where a third party owns migrations and therefore the only one whose recovery horizon is not ours to set.

idempotency_class.description: INV-P11-4. The runtime REFUSES to auto-retry the unsafe class. Default is `unsafe` — the safe failure direction — when the catalogue cannot determine the class.

consent_grade.description: INV-P11-6: consent is graded by CONSEQUENCE, not by resource, defaulting to the middle tier.
